items.name: Page-verdict cardinality: 8 values (C01) vs a 9th `not_assessable` (P08) vs `page_review_state` (X39)
items.situation: C01 keeps R-015 as locked (8 values). P08a adds a 9th verdict value `not_assessable`, excluded from denominators. X39 separately adds `page_review_state` with `no_usable_text` and `fetch_failed`, which already describe a page that cannot be assessed. A07 publishes `n_pages_by_verdict` as 8 counts and X29's truth table enumerates 8 values, so neither knows where a not-assessable page goes (negative set, unresolved, or excluded).
items.evidence: C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/t010/codebook-review/codebook-rulings-round1.json items C01 (chosen spec-locked), P08 (P08a), X39 (alt-1), A07 (add: '8 counts'), X29 (alt-1); C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:71 (R-015)

options.label: Keep 8 values; route non-assessability to X39
options.mechanism: Amend P08: `not_assessable` becomes a `page_review_state` value (e.g. `not_assessable_by_classifier` beside `no_usable_text`); the verdict column holds `_NA_` for any page not in state `reviewed`. X29 already treats non-reviewed states as unresolved.
options.benefits: C01 and R-015 stay as locked; one place records why a page has no verdict; A07 counts stay 8 plus X39 state counts.
options.risks: Procurement and text-detection channels must express their assessability outcome as a review state, not a verdict; a jev-judged 'unreadable' page and a pipeline failure share one column.
options.commits_to: P08 re-ruling; X39 enum gains a value; no verdict enum change beyond the planned v2.7 steps.

options.label: Adopt 9 values; trim X39
options.mechanism: Amend C01 / R-015 to 9 values with `not_assessable`; X39 keeps only pipeline states (`fetch_failed`, `link_not_followed_*`); A07 publishes 9 counts; X29 states whether `not_assessable` blocks `no`.
options.benefits: One verdict column answers 'what did we learn from this page' for every channel; matches P08 as ruled.
options.risks: Reopens a locked SPEC rule; the 9th value is unpiloted and may become an escape hatch for hard pages (P08's own risk); third enum change on the column.
options.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-015 (PI); two version steps; re-pilot of the verdict question; X29, A07 rewritten; procurement copy updated.

options.label: Keep both with a written boundary
options.mechanism: `not_assessable` = jev judges that the stored text cannot be assessed (e.g. only navigation, cookie wall); `no_usable_text` = deterministic pre-check failure. Both count as unresolved in X29; A07 counts 9 verdicts and the X39 states.
options.benefits: Keeps every ruling's intent.
options.risks: Two columns can disagree on the same page; the boundary is a new substantive definition that needs fixtures.
options.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-015; two version steps; fixtures for the boundary; X29/A07 text amended.

items.name: No downgrade target for low-confidence page verdicts other than `confirms_activity`
items.situation: R-081 says a page coded negative below threshold 'goes to unclear / unknown', but neither `unclear` nor `unknown` is one of the 8 verdict values. X14 alt-1 names only `confirms_activity` -> `ambiguous_genai`, which is also wrong when GenAI is clear but attribution lacks support (the natural target would be `ambiguous_attribution`). There is no target for low-confidence `no_genai`, `confirms_absence`, `background_only`, `event_only` or `other_body`, so X29 cannot tell a downgraded negative from a confident one unless it reads X40.
items.evidence: C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/SPEC.md:133 (R-081), :98 (R-041); C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/t010/codebook-review/codebook-rulings-round1.json items X14, X15, X29, X40; C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/t010/codebook-review/codebook-rulings-round1.json C01 risks ('`ambiguous_attribution` is collapsing')

options.label: Keep the code; carry the downgrade in `support_status`
options.mechanism: The verdict value is never rewritten; X40 `support_status` = `downgraded_low_confidence` / `downgraded_no_quote`. X29 treats any downgraded page as unresolved; publication shows the code with its status.
options.benefits: No enum change; the original jev answer stays analysable; X29 already lists unresolved signals.
options.risks: Users reading only the verdict column see un-downgraded codes; R-041's 'field to unknown' wording no longer literally applies to the verdict.
options.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-041/R-081 wording for the verdict; X29 and X40 text; no version steps for the verdict.

options.label: Per-value targets inside the 8 values
options.mechanism: Write a `downgrade_to` row for each value: `confirms_activity` -> `ambiguous_attribution` when the attribution quote fails, else `ambiguous_genai`; `other_body` -> `ambiguous_attribution`; `event_only`, `background_only`, `no_genai`, `confirms_absence` -> `ambiguous_genai`.
options.benefits: Stays within R-015; downgraded pages automatically enter pass 2 and the unresolved side of X29.
options.risks: Mixes 'page is ambiguous' with 'coder is unsure' in the same value, which distorts any analysis of ambiguous pages; downgraded negatives trigger pass-2 cost.
options.commits_to: X14 table rows (PI wording); fixtures; no enum change.

options.label: Add an `unresolved` verdict value
options.mechanism: Low-confidence or unsupported verdicts of any value go to `unresolved`.
options.benefits: Clean separation of coder uncertainty from page ambiguity.
options.risks: Breaks the 8-value lock; interacts with R2C01 (a 9th or 10th value); unpiloted.
options.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-015; Enum change: two contract-version steps (C-007), regenerated jev question set, contract-pin goldens, procurement enum copy (R-085 / D-008); X29 and A07 amended.

items.name: Group D applicability table (C06) names fields that other rulings replaced and misses the new ones
items.situation: C06 adds `not_applicable` to `tool_name`, `vendor`, `deployment_mode`, `target_users`, `access_type` and `interaction_type`, keyed on an action-type code. But C10 replaced `access_type` with `model_origin` and `build_arrangement` (neither has `not_applicable`), C11 replaced `interaction_type` with `interface` plus eight yes/no function items, C12 adds `model_name`, C17 splits `year_deployed`, C09 adds `procurement_status`, and A01, A09, P04 `supplier_role`, P06 `attribution_role` are new. C06 also does not say what applies when A02 is `unknown`, `program` or `procurement`.
items.evidence: C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/t010/codebook-review/codebook-rulings-round1.json items C06 (alt-1, commits 'Needs an action-type code (C08 alt-1 or A02)'), C10, C11, C12, C17, C09, A01, A02, A09, P04, P06

options.label: Full matrix keyed on A02
options.mechanism: Re-issue the C06 table as field x A02 value for every activity field, including the A02 values `unknown`, `program`, `procurement`; `not_applicable` added to every field the matrix can switch off.
options.benefits: Deterministic, complete, generator-friendly; jev is not asked inapplicable questions.
options.risks: Every A02 error now cascades to many fields; `unknown` rows need a default (ask all, or ask none).
options.commits_to: PI-signed matrix; Enum change: two contract-version steps (C-007), regenerated jev question set, contract-pin goldens, procurement enum copy (R-085 / D-008) for each field gaining `not_applicable`; fixtures per A02 value.

options.label: Matrix keyed on `activity_type` (C08, kept)
options.mechanism: Use the six v2.5 activity types as the key, since C08 was kept and is already in the series.
options.benefits: Comparable with v2.5 gating (`not_applicable` for `policy_guidance` already exists in interaction_type).
options.risks: activity_type has no procurement or training value (C08 risk), so those activities get the wrong applicability.
options.commits_to: PI-signed matrix; same enum steps as (a); A02's role in C06 removed.

options.label: Let jev decide applicability per field
options.mechanism: Add `not_applicable` as an answer option to each field's Choice question with a definition; no deterministic table.
options.benefits: No cascade from one action-type code; handles mixed activities.
options.risks: More questions answered; applicability becomes inconsistent across fields for the same activity; harder to test.
options.commits_to: Enum change: two contract-version steps (C-007), regenerated jev question set, contract-pin goldens, procurement enum copy (R-085 / D-008); re-pilot of the affected questions.

items.name: Missingness tokens differ across rulings for the same meaning
items.situation: 'Not asked because a gate excluded it' is `_NA_` in X02, X04 and X05 but `not_applicable` in C06, A03, A04 and C11 `interface`. 'Nothing stated' is `not_documented` (has_*), `none_documented` (C09 procurement_status), `none` (A09, C22, C23, X09 gates), `none_reported` (CX-60/61) and, after X14, `unknown` on yes/no items. No ruling defines a common grammar, so a generated data dictionary cannot say which tokens are structural, which are 'page silent' and which are 'coder could not decide'.
items.evidence: C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/t010/codebook-review/codebook-rulings-round1.json items C06, C09, C11, X02, X04, X05, X14, A03, A04, A09, C22, C23, X09; C:/Users/spaci/worktrees/G3O-integrator/g3o/extract/prompts/output_contract.md:88-92

options.label: One grammar for new and non-frozen fields
options.mechanism: Four reserved tokens: `_NA_` (gated out by rule), `not_documented` (page silent), `unknown` (stated but undeterminable, or downgraded), `not_applicable` merged into `_NA_`. New fields adopt them; frozen CX tokens keep their signed spelling and get a mapping row.
options.benefits: One reading rule for users and generators; fewer enum members.
options.risks: Renames values in several chosen options; v2.5 `not_applicable` in interaction_type becomes `_NA_` (crosswalk row).
options.commits_to: Enum spellings fixed before the v2.7 version steps (no extra steps if bundled); dictionary rule.

options.label: Keep per-field tokens; publish a class map
options.mechanism: Each token is mapped to a class (structural / silent / undeterminable / downgraded) in the codebook; the dictionary prints the class beside the token.
options.benefits: No renaming; chosen wording stands.
options.risks: Users must consult the map; QC rules must handle many spellings.

options.label: Keep `_NA_` and `not_applicable` as distinct, define both
options.mechanism: `_NA_` = the row or page is not an activity (verdict/gate); `not_applicable` = the activity exists but the field does not apply to its type.
options.benefits: Keeps a real distinction analysts may want.
options.risks: The X02/X04/X05 gates are field-level, so they would need `not_applicable` instead of `_NA_`, reopening those CX rulings.
options.commits_to: Re-signature of the CX `_NA_` additions or a written exception.

items.name: No order of operations for gated items, downgrades and blind quoting
items.situation: Many chosen options gate one item on another code: X02 on `disclosure_form`, X04 on post-downgrade `evaluation_documented`, X05 and X17 on the verdict, C06/A03/A04 on A02, C22/C23/X09 spans on a jev gate. C06 says gating is applied 'after jev, so jev is not asked inapplicable questions', which is only possible if the gating code is asked in an earlier round. X12 requires quotes before the code is seen and X35 checks them after, and X14/X15 downgrades can flip a gate. No ruling states the number of jev rounds per pass or when downgrades are applied.
items.evidence: C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/t010/codebook-review/codebook-rulings-round1.json items C06 mechanism, X04 mechanism, X12, X35, X14, X15; review-cx-support.json cross_cutting ('Pass-2 codes on non-confirming pages and downgrade cascades lack an order of operations')

options.label: Published round DAG
options.mechanism: Each codebook item carries `round` and `gate`; the pipeline runs gate items first, applies quote check, entailment and threshold downgrades, then asks dependent items. Indicatively pass 1: verdict -> (disclosure_form, source_type, completeness, content_*) -> disclosure_scope; pass 2: A02 + segmentation -> applicable fields -> gated spans and type items.
options.benefits: Gates mean what they say; fewer wasted questions; testable order.
options.risks: More requests and latency; a wrong gate code removes downstream answers entirely.
options.commits_to: Codebook columns; T-021/T-024 design change; cost re-estimate (T-002).

options.label: One round per pass, gates applied post hoc
options.mechanism: Ask every item in one round; void answers whose gate fails or was downgraded to `_NA_`.
options.benefits: Simplest pipeline; downgrades can be reapplied without re-asking.
options.risks: Pays for answers that are discarded; dependent items were answered without the gate's context (C06's stated aim is lost).
options.commits_to: Amend C06 and X04 mechanism text; cost re-estimate.

options.label: Hybrid
options.mechanism: Pre-gate only on the verdict (pass 1 -> pass 2) and on A02 (applicability); all other gates applied post hoc.
options.benefits: Captures most savings with two rounds per pass.
options.risks: Two rules for gating; X04 keeps its 'post-downgrade' dependency, so a second request remains there.
options.commits_to: Codebook columns; amend X02/X17 to post-hoc wording.

items.name: Outcomes and incidents have three competing gate/classification designs
items.situation: C22 gates outcomes with realised / expected / usage-only / none, then has CX-61 run on the extracted spans. X09 asks a separate gate quantified / qualitative / none on page text and makes CX-60 legacy-only. X10 runs CX-61 itself over page text with the span marked, and has the extractor quote support for the chosen value. C23 gates incidents by type (malfunction / breach / criticism / suspension / none) in one Choice although a page can report several, and `suspension or withdrawal` overlaps adoption_stage `discontinued` and the X24 `discontinued_uncertain` yes/no.
items.evidence: C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/t010/codebook-review/codebook-rulings-round1.json items C22, C23, X09, X10 (mechanisms), X24; H:/My Drive/Research/G3O/archive/planning-drive-copy-superseded-2026-10-26/launch-analysis-pr/index-design/codebook-extension-proposal.md:105-106

options.label: Two questions per field: substantive gate + CX-61 on page text
options.mechanism: Keep C22/C23 gates (realisation; incident type) and X10's CX-61 over page text; drop X09's separate existence question (CX-61 `none_reported` and the C22/C23 `none` agree by rule); spans extracted blind (X12).
options.benefits: Keeps both the new substantive distinctions and the signed CX-61 values.
options.risks: Two jev questions that can contradict (gate `none` but CX-61 `qualitative`); C23 single choice still loses multi-type pages unless it becomes yes/no items.
options.commits_to: Re-signature of CX-60/61 (X09/X10); C23 order rule or yes/no split; fixtures.

options.label: CX-61 over page text is the only gate
options.mechanism: Amend C22/C23 to spans only; X10 answers existence and kind; X09 folded into X10.
options.benefits: Fewest questions; one signed vocabulary.
options.risks: Loses realised vs expected and incident type, which C22/C23 were chosen to add.
options.commits_to: Re-ruling of C22/C23; re-signature of CX-61 grain (X10).

options.label: C22/C23 gates only, CX-61 derived on spans
options.mechanism: As C22 says: CX-61 runs on the extracted spans; amend X09/X10.
options.benefits: CX-61's input stays close to its signed 'stored text' input.
options.risks: CX-61 then depends on extraction quality and on blind quoting; reverses X10.
options.commits_to: Re-ruling of X09/X10; CX-61 stays signed as is for input but fixtures needed.

items.name: Quote length: no limit (C22) vs a cap at extraction applied to the API (X19)
items.situation: C22 stores outcome spans 'with no length limit in storage, display cap per R-043'. X19 alt-1 caps every quote at extraction and applies the same cap to the API and the site, which contradicts both C22 and R-043 as written. X25 truncates the snippet and X35 uses 'quote plus a short window', so four different length rules touch the same quotes.

options.label: Cap everywhere (X19), including outcome spans
options.mechanism: Amend C22: outcome and incident spans obey the X19 cap; long outcomes are split into several quotes.
options.benefits: One rule; cheaper storage and review.
options.risks: Long quantified results may be cut mid-sentence; CX-61 on spans (if retained) sees less text.
options.commits_to: C22 text; SPEC delta R-043 already owed by X19.

options.label: Cap with field-level exemptions
options.mechanism: X19 cap for all quotes except outcome/incident spans, which are stored in full and display-capped.
options.benefits: Keeps C22's intent for the evidence most likely to be long.
options.risks: Two regimes in one quote table; API consumers see uneven lengths.

options.label: Revert to R-043 as written
options.mechanism: Full text stored and in the API; cap on the website only (DEC-016 c); X19 reconsidered.
options.benefits: No information loss; matches a prior PI ruling.
options.risks: Reopens X19; long verbatim text in a public API raises the reuse concern flagged in review-cx-support cross_cutting.

items.name: Blind quoting (X12) vs rulings that give the extractor the code
items.situation: X12 has the extractor quote the passages relevant to each field without being told jev's value. X10 has the extractor 'quote support for the chosen value', A01 has it 'return the supporting quote' for a mechanism value, and C22/C23 extract spans only 'unless none', which needs the gate result first. A09 and X26 make the extractor a primary coder of a value (number span, date) rather than a blind quoter.
items.evidence: C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/t010/codebook-review/codebook-rulings-round1.json items X12, X10, A01, C22, C23, A09, X26

options.label: Value-blind, gate-aware
options.mechanism: Define blind as: the extractor never sees the value of the field it quotes for, but may see that a gate is not `none`. Amend X10 and A01 to field-relevant quotes; A09/X26 listed as extractor-primary fields with R-042 checks.
options.benefits: Keeps X12's protection against confirmation; workable with the gates.
options.risks: Gate-awareness still signals that something exists; the definition is a new rule.
options.commits_to: SPEC delta to R-040 (already owed by X12); X10/A01 text.

options.label: Blind only for enum codes
options.mechanism: Blind for verdict and Group D/CX enums; value-aware for spans, dates and numbers.
options.benefits: Simple; spans and numbers are the extractor's own output anyway.
options.risks: A01 and X10 quotes become confirmatory, which X35 then checks with the same bias.

options.label: Fully blind, gates after
options.mechanism: Extractor returns outcome/incident/scale spans unconditionally; jev gates afterwards; spans with gate `none` are discarded.
options.benefits: Strict independence between quote and code.
options.risks: Extraction runs and spends on every activity; more false spans to discard.

items.name: Safeguard items: four-value `has_*` (C18-C21) vs derived yes/not_documented (X07)
items.situation: C18-C21 define `has_*` with four values (yes / no / unclear / not_documented) and an attachment rule. X07 asks each safeguard once per (page x activity) and derives activity `has_*` as yes / not_documented and page `content_*` as 'any activity yes', which drops `no` and `unclear`. X07 covers three safeguards; `content_user_notification` (CX W1 = a: a described notice or label) is narrower than `has_transparency_notice` ('are users notified that GenAI is involved'), and `has_data_classification` has no CX counterpart. Pages with GenAI content but no segmented activity get no `content_*` safeguard value. P05a adds a third human-oversight item (contract clause).

options.label: Shared four-value question
options.mechanism: One pass-2 question per safeguard with the C18-C21 values; activity `has_*` = the answer; page `content_*` = yes if any activity yes, else no. Notification uses the CX W1 definition and `has_transparency_notice` is re-worded to it; `has_data_classification` stays Group D only; P05 contract clauses tagged as a governance-activity answer.
options.benefits: One question, one definition; `no`/`unclear` kept.
options.risks: Re-signs CX-52's grain (page -> derived); v2.5 has_transparency_notice series changes meaning.
options.commits_to: Re-signature of CX-52; wording step for C19; fixtures; P05 grain note.

options.label: Binary as in X07
options.mechanism: Amend C18-C21 to yes / not_documented (plus X14 `unknown`); drop `no` and `unclear`.
options.benefits: Aligns with CX yes/no; simpler.
options.risks: Loses stated absence ('no human review') and mixed cases; v2.5 `no`/`unclear` rows cannot be represented.
options.commits_to: Enum change: two contract-version steps (C-007), regenerated jev question set, contract-pin goldens, procurement enum copy (R-085 / D-008) on four fields; crosswalk rows for v2.5 `no`/`unclear`.

options.label: Keep two instruments
options.mechanism: content_* stay pass-1 page items per CX-52; has_* stay pass-2 per C18-C21; publish a concordance QC.
options.benefits: No re-signature of CX; each instrument keeps its pilot basis.
options.risks: Twice the questions; two public answers to one question can disagree.

items.name: `deployment_mode` (C14) and `interface` (C11) code the same distinction

options.risks: Re-drafts C11's chosen values; unpiloted.
options.commits_to: Enum change: two contract-version steps (C-007), regenerated jev question set, contract-pin goldens, procurement enum copy (R-085 / D-008); re-pilot of interface.

options.label: Keep both with a QC constraint

options.benefits: No re-ruling.
options.risks: Extra question; flags will be common where wording differs.

items.name: Three overlapping typologies: activity_type (kept), action_type (A02), stage + procurement_status (C09)
items.situation: C08 kept the six v2.5 activity types, which mix kind, stage and audience and have no procurement or training value. A02 adds action_type (deployment / procurement / governance / staff_training / proposal / program / unknown). C09 keeps adoption_stage (with `proposed`) and adds procurement_status. Nothing rules out contradictory combinations (activity_type `pilot_experiment` with action_type `governance`; action_type `procurement` with procurement_status `none_documented`; action_type `proposal` with stage `production`), and A02's own note leaves 'proposal as type or stage' to the PI. A02 `program` also overlaps C07 'components of a named program' and the X30 relation `component_of_program`.
items.evidence: C:/Users/spaci/repos/G3O/planning/t010/codebook-review/codebook-rulings-round1.json items C08 (keep), A02 (add; mechanism note on `proposal`), C09 (alt-2), C07, X30

options.label: Keep all three; publish cross-field constraints
options.mechanism: A constraint table lists allowed combinations; violations trigger a QC flag or a downgrade of the lower-confidence code.
options.benefits: No re-ruling; series continuity for activity_type.
options.risks: Three questions per activity on overlapping constructs; reliability of the multi-dimensional activity_type stays low.

options.label: Derive activity_type from A02 + stage + users
options.mechanism: activity_type computed by a published crosswalk (e.g. governance -> policy_guidance; deployment + pilot -> pilot_experiment; deployment + public users -> public_facing_service); jev not asked.
options.benefits: One fewer question; no contradictions by construction; v2.5 column still filled.
options.risks: Derived activity_type differs from v2.5 jev-coded values (series break disguised as continuity); some cells do not map.
options.commits_to: Crosswalk table; C08 re-ruling; data dictionary note.

options.label: Make A02 orthogonal
